Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zugodb 0.0.0.9000

  • dbWriteTableArrow(), dbAppendTableArrow() and dbCreateTableArrow() take an Arrow C stream from any producer (a stream handle from zuarrow, nanoarrow, arrow or an ADBC driver, or a data frame with zuarrow installed) and load it into a table batch by batch, with no data frame in between. The stream is read once and released. A column of a type the engine cannot hold (a decimal, a time, a list, a struct, a dictionary, …) is a zug_type_error naming it, before any row is read; a producer’s error is a new zug_stream_error. A load that fails part-way leaves nothing: an append or an overwrite goes through a staging table first.

  • The engine is libzugodb 0.4.0 (it was 0.1.1). What changes for users:

    • SQL reads and writes no file: every file table function (read_csv(), read_parquet(), read_json(), …), a file path used as a table, DESCRIBE of one, COPY to or from a file and CREATE LIVE VIEW are a zug_sql_error, “Reading or writing files from SQL is not supported”. Files come back through the zu family’s readers (design §7).
    • A database file is format 1001, with a checksum. A file written by earlier versions of zugodb (format 1), a damaged one, a truncated one and one that is not a database are each a zug_sql_error when opened, and are left as they were.
    • DuckDB’s answers where SlothDB’s differed: names match ignoring case, TINYINT arithmetic overflows as an error, substr() counts characters, a BLOB literal’s \x escapes are bytes, Infinity fits a FLOAT column, a NaN written is stored and read back as NaN, and many wrong answers are fixed (libzugodb’s CHANGELOG.md).
    • BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK are refused, and HUGEINT, INTERVAL, UUID and DECIMAL are refused by SQL. TIME values are right now, and still a zug_type_error when read (#43).
    • dbExecute() of CREATE TABLE ... AS returns the rows it made.
    • The package bundles no zstd, snappy, fastpforlib or miniz.

  • The package is renamed from zuslothdb to zugodb, and its repository to pedrobtz/zugodb (design D12). The driver is zugodb(), zuslothdb_info() is zug_info(), the classes are zugodb_driver, zugodb_connection and zugodb_result, the conditions are zug_error, zug_sql_error, zug_type_error, zug_unsupported, zug_closed_error and zug_argument_error, and the test switches are ZUG_SKIP_HEAVY, ZUG_SLOW_TESTS and ZUG_TEST_SEED. Nothing else changes.

  • The engine is now libzugodb (https://github.com/pedrobtz/libzugodb), this package’s own fork of SlothDB, vendored by release tag. Its 0.1.1 fixes a data race on every multi-threaded Parquet scan, which UBSan under libstdc++ 15 stopped as “unreachable program point”. zug_info() reports its tag and the SlothDB commit it descends from (origin, origin_commit), and no longer a list of changes. Nothing else changes.

  • SQLite, Excel and Avro files are not supported: SlothDB’s readers for the first two returned wrong values against real files, and its Avro reader is untested. sqlite_scan(), read_xlsx(), read_avro() and their file extensions are an error saying so (#55).

  • Arrow IPC files are not supported: SlothDB’s Arrow format is its own, and reads no file another Arrow tool writes. read_arrow() and a .arrow, .feather or .ipc path are an error saying so (#40).

  • A JSON file the engine would read wrongly is an error naming the record and the key: a nested object or array, a key the first record does not have, or a value whose type is not the first record’s for that key. Before, such values were dropped or coerced (#39). \u escapes are decoded.

  • A Parquet column the engine would read wrongly is an error naming it, when a query uses it: DECIMAL (read unscaled), TIME, millisecond and nanosecond TIMESTAMP (read as raw counts), UUID and INTERVAL (read as NULL), and unsigned 32- and 64-bit integers (read as signed). Queries on the file’s other columns work (#36, #37, #38).

  • dbWriteTable(), dbAppendTable(), dbListTables(), dbListFields(), dbExistsTable(), dbRemoveTable(), dbDataType() and dbQuoteIdentifier() write and manage tables. Logical, integer, double, character, factor, Date, POSIXct, integer64 and blob columns are written and read back identical; a column of another class, or a value its column cannot hold, is a zug_type_error before any row is written.

  • SlothDB has no transactions, so dbBegin(), dbCommit() and dbRollback() are zug_unsupported, and SQL ROLLBACK is an error saying that nothing was undone.

  • A table of more than 2048 rows with a NULL past row 2048 no longer reads back with NULLs where there are none, or crashes R: the engine kept a whole row group’s NULLs in a mask the size of one vector, and an INSERT of more than 2048 VALUES wrote past its buffers (#45).

  • DATE columns arrive as Date, TIMESTAMP as POSIXct and BLOB as a list of raw vectors with blob::blob()’s classes. dbConnect(timezone_out = ) sets the time zone a POSIXct is shown in, "UTC" by default as in duckdb; an unknown zone is an error.

  • A HUGEINT or TIME column is a zug_type_error, since SlothDB computes their values wrongly (a TIME is always midnight), as are INTERVAL and UUID. SlothDB produces no DECIMAL, time zone, list, struct, map or union column.

  • A set operation (UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) returns TINYINT, SMALLINT and FLOAT columns with their values; it returned numbers made of unwritten memory (#41).

  • On Windows, a Parquet query on more than one thread that decodes several row groups no longer ends the R session (#34).

  • A Parquet query that stops before the file’s last row group, such as a LIMIT, no longer hangs now and then: the engine’s decode workers could miss the signal to stop (#32).

  • dbSendQuery(), dbFetch(), dbGetQuery() and the other result methods return data frames. Boolean, integer, floating-point and VARCHAR columns arrive as logical, integer, double and UTF-8 character; dbConnect(bigint = ) chooses double, integer64 or character for 64-bit integers. A value R cannot hold exactly is a zug_type_error, never a silent change.

  • dbExecute() no longer reads a query’s one-row BIGINT column named Count as a row count.

  • zugodb() is a DBI driver, used as duckdb::duckdb() is: it holds one database, in memory or in a file, that its connections share. dbConnect(), dbDisconnect(), dbIsValid(), dbGetInfo() and show() work for the driver and the connection, and dbExecute() runs statements and returns the rows they changed.

  • dbConnect(read_only = TRUE) refuses every statement that would change the database and never writes its file.

  • dbConnect(threads = ) caps the engine’s threads, 2 by default; the engine has one thread pool per process, so the cap is process-wide.

  • A file database is written when its last connection closes. A connection used in a forked child is a zug_closed_error.

  • Errors are conditions inheriting from zug_error: zug_sql_error (the engine’s message), zug_type_error, zug_argument_error, zug_closed_error and zug_unsupported (params =).

  • The SlothDB engine is bundled and compiled with the package, from pedrobtz/slothdb, zugodb’s fork of SlothDB: upstream commit 8180f21 and zugodb’s changes to it, listed by zug_info(). The package is offline only: a remote path in a query is an error.
